title: Why Your Car Smells Damp or Musty (and How to Fix It)
meta_description: A damp, musty car smell means water is trapped in the carpet, boot or air con. How to find the source, dry it out yourself, and when it needs extraction.
excerpt: A musty smell means water is sitting somewhere in the car. Here's how to find it, what you can dry out yourself, and what it takes when the damp has soaked in.

hero.alt: Rear seats and footwell of a hatchback with grey fabric seats and a vacuumed carpet mat

faq.q: Why does my car smell musty when I turn the fan on?
faq.a: That usually points to the cabin air filter or the air conditioning system staying damp. Changing an old filter is the first thing to try. If the smell carries on, the ventilation needs treating, not just the surfaces.

faq.q: Will an air freshener get rid of a damp smell?
faq.a: No. It covers the smell for a while, but the water and mould causing it are still there. The smell comes back once the scent fades or the car warms up.

faq.q: How do I know if my car carpet is wet underneath?
faq.a: Take the mats out and press your palm firmly into the carpet, especially in the footwells and near the doors. The top can feel dry while the underlay beneath it is still wet.

faq.q: Can you fix the leak that's letting water in?
faq.a: No, we clean and treat the inside of the car but don't repair seals or bodywork. If water is still getting in, have the leak fixed at a garage or bodyshop first, or the smell will come back.

A damp or musty smell in your car almost always means water is sitting somewhere it shouldn't: in the carpet underlay, the boot floor or the air con. An air freshener won't touch it, because the source is still there.

This time of year it's usually wet shoes, damp coats and misty windows, but blocked drains and tired seals are common too. Our new guide covers how to find where the smell is coming from, what you can dry out yourself, and when it needs proper extraction.

Car smells musty? Take the mats out and press your hand firmly into the carpet underneath 🍂

The top can feel dry while the thick underlay below is still wet, and that's where the smell comes from. Dry the mats indoors, soak up what you can with towels, and leave the doors open on a dry day. If it's soaked through or keeps coming back, it needs extraction, not an air freshener.
